answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. Votes are weighted by locked stake, and deposits are slashed when a fraud challenge is upheld, so spinning up a spiral of sockpuppets does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it. A comet of short-lived accounts or a plume of coordinated reviews still faces the same per-account bond, making Sybil influence costly rather than impossible.
